sourceLessons.title: Connect a model on your computer
sourceLessons.prerequisites: A downloaded local model, or the first-run automatic setup. Enough disk space and memory for that model.

steps.title: Understand the two local routes
steps.narrationDraft: Ollama manages downloaded models by name. llama.cpp loads a model file, usually ending in .gguf. Both can run the brain on your computer. Downloading a model initially needs internet; after setup, local inference can work offline. Internet tools still need internet.
steps.checkpoint: You have chosen Ollama or llama.cpp.

steps.title: Open Models and create a template
steps.narrationDraft: Open Settings → Models → New. Give the template an easy name such as “My everyday local model.” A template, also called a preset, is a saved model connection and its settings. Choosing a preset later saves you from typing the connection again.
steps.checkpoint: The New template window is open.

steps.title: For Ollama, match the model name
steps.narrationDraft: Choose Ollama (local). Keep the local endpoint if Ollama is on this computer. Enter the exact installed model name. The example qwen3:8b only works when that model is installed in Ollama. Genesis’s automatic welcome setup can download a model for you; typing a name in Models does not download it.
steps.checkpoint: The model name matches an installed Ollama model.
steps.tip: An endpoint is the address of the model service. “127.0.0.1” means this computer.

steps.title: For llama.cpp, choose your GGUF file
steps.narrationDraft: Choose llama.cpp (local). Enter the GGUF model path and check the endpoint. Genesis can load a configured local model when selected. If you already run your own server, use its address and matching model setup. GPU layers controls how much work goes to the graphics card; start with the supplied settings.
steps.checkpoint: The file path points to an existing GGUF model.

steps.title: Save a modest starting configuration
steps.narrationDraft: Leave the model’s recommended generation settings in place. Large context sizes and large models need more memory. A context number in Genesis does not give a model more capacity than its server or hardware supports. Save the template, choose it, and press Save changes in the Models page.
steps.checkpoint: The selected primary is the local model you configured.

steps.title: Say hello and check the answer

anchor.label: Choose primary model from saved templates

steps.narrationDraft: Return to Conversation and send a short hello. If it cannot connect, check that the local model service is running, the address is right and the name matches. If it is very slow or runs out of memory, try a smaller model or smaller supported context.
steps.checkpoint: A real answer arrives from your local model.

sourceLessons.title: Connect a cloud model
sourceLessons.prerequisites: An account and API key from the provider you chose. Internet access.

steps.title: Choose where answers will come from
steps.narrationDraft: Open Settings → Models. The provider choices include NVIDIA Cloud, Nebius Token Factory, Anthropic, and Custom (OpenAI-compatible). Custom is for a service that accepts the compatible API format. A chat website subscription and an API account may be separate; use the key for the service’s API.
steps.checkpoint: You have selected the provider you actually have access to.

steps.title: Keep the connection details together
steps.narrationDraft: Choose a matching preset or make a new template. For providers with an Endpoint URL, use the base address supplied by that provider. Enter the exact Model name available to your API account. Example names and example URLs are placeholders, not a working account.
steps.checkpoint: Provider, endpoint and model name all belong to the same service.

steps.title: Enter your key in its own field
steps.narrationDraft: Paste the provider’s API key into the key field on the Models page. Keys are stored separately from templates. Do not put your real key in a screenshot or shared example. Parse code does not fill the key field; a copied example is not a substitute for entering the key here.
steps.checkpoint: The provider key field reports that a key is set after saving.

steps.title: Use the provider’s supported settings
steps.narrationDraft: Start with a supplied preset or the provider’s example connection code. Some providers do not accept every generation control. A disabled parameter switch leaves that form parameter out where supported. Provider-specific thinking profiles belong to the matching model, not every model you own.
steps.checkpoint: Your settings match what the provider supports.

steps.title: Save and try a short request

anchor.label: Choose primary model from saved templates

steps.narrationDraft: Click Save changes, return to Conversation and send a short request. A wrong model name, expired key, exhausted quota or incorrect address can prevent a reply. Check those first. The Backup lesson shows how a second model can help when the primary becomes unavailable.
steps.checkpoint: You receive an answer before trying a larger task.
steps.tip: Cloud usage may have charges or limits set by the provider. Genesis’s activity totals are not your provider’s bill.

sourceLessons.title: Add a model by pasting connection code
sourceLessons.prerequisites: A provider’s example Python, cURL, Node or compatible connection snippet. Use an example without your real secret.

steps.title: Start with the provider and key
steps.narrationDraft: Open Settings → Models and choose the right provider, or use New for a separate template. Enter the actual API key in the provider’s key field. The parser reads the example as text; it does not run the pasted program, install a model or create a provider account.
steps.checkpoint: You are editing the intended provider or template.

steps.title: Open the optional code panel
steps.narrationDraft: Find Paste connection code (optional) and click Show. Paste the provider’s connection example. It can contain the model name, base URL and request settings. The example in this tutorial uses a deliberately nonworking example address and key placeholder. For your model, copy the provider’s real documented values.
steps.checkpoint: The connection snippet is visible in the text box.

steps.title: Click Parse code and review the result
steps.narrationDraft: Click Parse code. Genesis extracts values it recognises, redacts key text in the saved snippet, and shows detected information or warnings. When it finds a model and base URL, those fill the relevant form fields. Image capability and thinking profiles can also be detected. Check the result; unusual code may not be fully understood.
steps.checkpoint: The imported checklist contains the values you expected.
steps.tip: Do not assume the parser chose a different provider for you. Check the provider yourself. It never reads the real API key into the key field.

steps.title: Understand which value will be sent
steps.narrationDraft: With Apply pasted parameters to this model on, each checked imported key wins over the matching form value. In our example, imported temperature = 0.7 wins even if the temperature field still displays 0.3. The field can be dimmed and labelled “Pasted code applies temperature.” The summary labels imported values “pasted.”
steps.checkpoint: You can identify the value that will actually control the next request.
steps.tip: Temperature affects how varied answers are. The pasted value is active; a visible old slider value is not necessarily the value being sent.

steps.title: Give one setting back to its slider
steps.narrationDraft: To control temperature from the normal form again, uncheck temperature in the imported checklist. Then enable and adjust the form’s Temperature control. Other checked imported keys still apply. To stop using all pasted parameters together, turn off the master Apply pasted parameters switch.
steps.checkpoint: Only the imported keys you want remain active.

steps.title: Know the separate settings
steps.narrationDraft: Imported max_tokens or max_completion_tokens can replace the form’s output limit. seed may have no normal slider. The Context window is Genesis’s prompt budget and local-server setting; it is not simply another pasted request parameter. Active thinking ON/OFF profiles can override pasted thinking-related settings when thinking changes.
steps.checkpoint: You know which settings are separate from the imported checklist.

steps.title: Save both the configuration and the template you need
steps.narrationDraft: Check the provider, URL, model name, key status and imported values. In an existing Models form, Save changes applies the edited configuration. Update template saves changes back into the selected reusable template. In a New template window, use Create template, then Save changes on the Models page. Test a short message.
steps.checkpoint: The chosen model answers with the saved configuration.

steps.title: Switch models without carrying the old example along
steps.narrationDraft: When you select a different saved preset, its own settings replace the model-specific pasted configuration. Old presets without imported values receive neutral defaults. Keep separate presets for different models. Clear removes the imported snippet and keys; review any separately detected thinking profiles or image capability afterward.
steps.checkpoint: Each preset has the connection and parameters intended for that model.

sourceLessons.title: Understand model settings
sourceLessons.prerequisites: Settings → Models open. Start with a working preset.

steps.title: Context is the model’s working desk
steps.narrationDraft: Context window is how much text can fit into one model request: instructions, conversation, memories and tools. Max output tokens limits one generated reply. A token is a small piece of text, not necessarily a whole word. More output leaves less room for input within the total window.
steps.checkpoint: You can distinguish the input workspace from the length of one answer.

steps.title: Use a size your model can really handle
steps.narrationDraft: Genesis checks model limits and local memory where possible. Trust my context window overrides some local safeguards; use it only when both the server and hardware support your chosen size. Context framing reserve keeps room for chat and tool formatting. Turning off the form’s context switch does not remove Genesis’s internal safe prompt budget.
steps.checkpoint: The context choice agrees with your model and server.

steps.title: Variety and repetition controls
steps.narrationDraft: Temperature adjusts variation. Top-P and Top-K adjust which possible next words can be considered. Presence penalty and Repeat penalty affect repetition when supported. These are optional fine-tuning controls. Keep the model’s recommended values until you have a specific problem to solve.
steps.checkpoint: You know what these controls broadly mean without needing to change them.

steps.title: Reasoning and streaming
steps.narrationDraft: The reasoning chooser appears according to the model’s abilities. Use profile follows the saved configuration; supported models may offer Off, Low, Medium or High. Stream mode shows words as they arrive; off waits for a full reply. Streaming changes presentation, not whether Genesis can use tools.
steps.checkpoint: You can choose a supported reasoning level and recognise streaming.

steps.title: Advanced profiles and mood-following thinking
steps.narrationDraft: Advanced thinking profiles and Custom reasoning levels describe provider-specific request settings. Use the provider’s supported values; invented level names do not give a model new abilities. Thinking follows mood, when enabled, adjusts effort within your selected ceiling for supported models. It does not add reasoning levels to a model that has none.
steps.checkpoint: You understand why some controls are unavailable for a particular model.

sourceLessons.title: Keep going with a backup model
sourceLessons.prerequisites: Two working saved model presets. A local backup can work when a cloud service is unavailable.

steps.title: Save the backup first
steps.narrationDraft: Connect and test your second model, then save it as a preset. A backup must be able to answer on its own. Selecting an uninstalled local model or a cloud model without a valid key will not provide a working backup.
steps.checkpoint: Both the primary and backup have answered a small test.

steps.title: Choose Backup model
steps.narrationDraft: Open Settings → Models → Companion failover — not Missions. Choose the second preset under Backup model and click Save changes. This covers Chat, Work, Autonomy and companion helpers. The compact Backup chooser below the Modern message box also selects a saved backup.
steps.checkpoint: The backup status reports standby or current fallback use.

steps.title: Know what makes it switch

anchor.label: Using backup: Qwen3 8B (Ollama). Next request will retry primary.

steps.narrationDraft: If the primary fails before delivering an answer—for example because of a provider usage limit, rate limit, timeout or outage—Genesis can retry through the configured backup. It carries the working request forward. Content or tool work already delivered is not blindly replayed on the backup, so fallback is not a promise that every partial failure can be recovered.
steps.checkpoint: You recognise the backup status when the demonstration shows it.

steps.title: Your primary choice stays saved

anchor.label: Using backup: Qwen3 8B (Ollama). Next request will retry primary.

steps.narrationDraft: The primary’s saved connection remains your primary. The status explains which model is actually answering, separately from your chosen primary. Your backup might be less capable: a smaller local model may give a simpler answer, and it may need a separate vision helper for pictures.
steps.checkpoint: You can tell a configured primary from the effective backup.

steps.title: Return happens on a real request
steps.narrationDraft: Retry primary after (minutes) is the cooldown. After it passes, the next real request tests the primary. Success returns to primary; failure starts another waiting period. Genesis does not make a paid background ping just because the timer expires. A backend restart starts with the saved primary again.
steps.checkpoint: You understand why the status can say the next request will retry.

steps.title: Missions have a separate backup for each role
steps.narrationDraft: Open Settings → Missions → Role models for mission primary and backup choices. The companion backup does not govern Missions. Each role may use a different model and has its own failover window for provider rate limits. Check these before a big job.
steps.checkpoint: You know where to set the mission’s independent model choices.
steps.tip: Usage limits are different from a full context window or a task’s step budget. A backup does not remove those other limits.

audio.rationale: Video-3 decoded envelope: retain its original opening once; repeats enter at the first strong 7.5s section. Use a 224s musical span and 8s overlap (216s repeat spacing); omit the descending near-silent ending after 237s. Equal-power overlaps cover the final 223.5–231.5s phrase with the incoming 7.5–15.5s phrase. Four-second opening and eight-second final fades, calm -20 LUFS target. Instrumented envelope inspection; no continuous subjective-listening claim.

check this
items: You are editing the intended provider or template.
scenes.note: Try it in Genesis. Pause for as long as you need. Continue when you can explain or confirm this result.

scenes.title:
Show the
code panel
scenes.body: Find Paste connection code (optional) and click Show. Paste the provider’s connection example. It can contain the model name, base URL and request settings.
scenes.note: Step 2 of 8 · Teaching 1 of 2. Locate the highlighted control.

scenes.title:
Show the
code panel
scenes.body: The example in this tutorial uses a deliberately nonworking example address and key placeholder. For your model, copy the provider’s real documented values.
scenes.note: Step 2 of 8 · Teaching 2 of 2. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
Read the
example first
items: base_url = https://api.example.com/v1
model = your-model-name
api_key = YOUR_API_KEY
temperature = 0.7; max_tokens = 4096; seed = 42
scenes.note: Deliberately nonworking example values. Use your provider’s documented address and model; keep a placeholder here.

scenes.title:
Pause and
check this
items: The connection snippet is visible in the text box.
scenes.note: Try it in Genesis. Pause for as long as you need. Continue when you can explain or confirm this result.

scenes.title:
Parse, then
review
scenes.body: Click Parse code. Genesis extracts values it recognises, redacts key text in the saved snippet, and shows detected information or warnings.
scenes.note: Step 3 of 8 · Teaching 1 of 3. Locate the highlighted control.

scenes.title:
Parse, then
review
scenes.body: When it finds a model and base URL, those fill the relevant form fields. Image capability and thinking profiles can also be detected.
scenes.note: Step 3 of 8 · Teaching 2 of 3. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
Parse, then
review
scenes.body: Check the result; unusual code may not be fully understood.
scenes.note: Step 3 of 8 · Teaching 3 of 3. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
A useful
detail
items: Do not assume the parser chose a different provider for you. Check the provider yourself.
It never reads the real API key into the key field.
scenes.note: Keep this distinction in mind as you practice.

scenes.title:
Review what
was detected
items: Confirm the provider yourself
Review detected model and base URL
Read warnings and the imported checklist
Check any detected vision or thinking profiles
scenes.note: The saved snippet redacts recognised key text. The parser never fills the actual provider API key field.

scenes.title:
Pause and
check this
items: The imported checklist contains the values you expected.
scenes.note: Try it in Genesis. Pause for as long as you need. Continue when you can explain or confirm this result.

scenes.title:
Which value
will be sent?
scenes.body: With Apply pasted parameters to this model on, each checked imported key wins over the matching form value.
scenes.note: Step 4 of 8 · Teaching 1 of 3. Locate the highlighted control.

scenes.title:
Which value
will be sent?
scenes.body: In our example, imported temperature = 0.7 wins even if the temperature field still displays 0.3.
scenes.note: Step 4 of 8 · Teaching 2 of 3. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
Which value
will be sent?
scenes.body: The field can be dimmed and labelled “Pasted code applies temperature.” The summary labels imported values “pasted.”
scenes.note: Step 4 of 8 · Teaching 3 of 3. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
A useful
detail
items: Temperature affects how varied answers are.
The pasted value is active; a visible old slider value is not necessarily the value being sent.
scenes.note: Keep this distinction in mind as you practice.

scenes.title:
The 0.7 / 0.3
example
items: Imported temperature: 0.7, checked
Apply pasted parameters: on
Form temperature: 0.3, dimmed
Effective temperature for the request: 0.7
scenes.note: Pause: which wins? The checked imported 0.7 wins over the matching form value. Genesis does not average them.

scenes.title:
Pause and
check this
items: You can identify the value that will actually control the next request.
scenes.note: Try it in Genesis. Pause for as long as you need. Continue when you can explain or confirm this result.

scenes.title:
Return control
to the form
scenes.body: To control temperature from the normal form again, uncheck temperature in the imported checklist. Then enable and adjust the form’s Temperature control.
scenes.note: Step 5 of 8 · Teaching 1 of 2. Locate the highlighted control.

scenes.title:
Return control
to the form
scenes.body: Other checked imported keys still apply. To stop using all pasted parameters together, turn off the master Apply pasted parameters switch.
scenes.note: Step 5 of 8 · Teaching 2 of 2. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
Give just one
control back
items: Uncheck temperature in the imported checklist
Enable the form’s Temperature control
Set the form value you actually want
Leave other wanted imported keys checked
scenes.note: Turning off the master Apply pasted parameters switch stops the whole imported overlay. Enable the form controls you need.

scenes.title:
Pause and
check this
items: Only the imported keys you want remain active.
scenes.note: Try it in Genesis. Pause for as long as you need. Continue when you can explain or confirm this result.

scenes.title:
Separate
settings
scenes.body: Imported max_tokens or max_completion_tokens can replace the form’s output limit. seed may have no normal slider.
scenes.note: Step 6 of 8 · Teaching 1 of 3. Locate the highlighted control.

scenes.title:
Separate
settings
scenes.body: The Context window is Genesis’s prompt budget and local-server setting; it is not simply another pasted request parameter.
scenes.note: Step 6 of 8 · Teaching 2 of 3. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
Separate
settings
scenes.body: Active thinking ON/OFF profiles can override pasted thinking-related settings when thinking changes.
scenes.note: Step 6 of 8 · Teaching 3 of 3. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
Output and
context differ
items: max_tokens / max_completion_tokens: reply limit
seed: may have no matching form slider
Context window: prompt budget and local-server setup
Thinking ON/OFF profiles: separate active overrides
scenes.note: Changing thinking can select a profile that overrides static pasted thinking settings. Review the matching profile.

scenes.title:
Pause and
check this
items: You know which settings are separate from the imported checklist.
scenes.note: Try it in Genesis. Pause for as long as you need. Continue when you can explain or confirm this result.

scenes.title:
Save the form
and template
scenes.body: Check the provider, URL, model name, key status and imported values. In an existing Models form, Save changes applies the edited configuration.
scenes.note: Step 7 of 8 · Teaching 1 of 2. Locate the highlighted control.

scenes.title:
Save the form
and template
scenes.body: Update template saves changes back into the selected reusable template. In a New template window, use Create template, then Save changes on the Models page. Test a short message.
scenes.note: Step 7 of 8 · Teaching 2 of 2. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
Two places
to save
items: Save changes: apply the edited Models form
Update template: keep edits in the reusable preset
New: Create template, then Models → Save changes
Test one short message after saving
scenes.note: Before saving, verify provider, URL, exact model, key status and active imported values together.

scenes.title:
Pause and
check this
items: The chosen model answers with the saved configuration.
scenes.note: Try it in Genesis. Pause for as long as you need. Continue when you can explain or confirm this result.

scenes.title:
Each preset
is independent
scenes.body: When you select a different saved preset, its own settings replace the model-specific pasted configuration. Old presets without imported values receive neutral defaults.
scenes.note: Step 8 of 8 · Teaching 1 of 2. Locate the highlighted control.

scenes.title:
Each preset
is independent
scenes.body: Keep separate presets for different models. Clear removes the imported snippet and keys; review any separately detected thinking profiles or image capability afterward.
scenes.note: Step 8 of 8 · Teaching 2 of 2. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
Keep model A
and B separate
items: Save model A’s connection and imported settings
Choose model B’s own saved preset
Check that B has B’s intended configuration
Clear removes the imported snippet and keys
scenes.note: After Clear, review separately detected thinking profiles and image capability. They may need their own adjustment.

scenes.title:
Pause and
check this
items: Each preset has the connection and parameters intended for that model.
scenes.note: Try it in Genesis. Pause for as long as you need. Continue when you can explain or confirm this result.

complete

scenes.title:
Know your
model controls.
scenes.body:
Understand model settings
Context, output, variation and supported thinking.

scenes.title:
Before
you begin
items: Settings → Models open. Start with a working preset.
scenes.note: These are the prerequisites for this lesson. Prepare them before you try the connection.

scenes.title:
Your model’s
working desk
scenes.body: Context window is how much text can fit into one model request: instructions, conversation, memories and tools. Max output tokens limits one generated reply.
scenes.note: Step 1 of 5 · Teaching 1 of 2. Locate the highlighted control.

scenes.title:
Your model’s
working desk
scenes.body: A token is a small piece of text, not necessarily a whole word. More output leaves less room for input within the total window.
scenes.note: Step 1 of 5 · Teaching 2 of 2. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
A working-desk
example
items: Example total context: 8,192 tokens
Example output limit: 1,024 tokens
Example framing reserve: 512 tokens
Input must also leave room for output and framing
scenes.note: Illustrative arithmetic leaves at most 6,656 tokens before other constraints. A token is a piece of text, not a word.

scenes.title:
Pause and
check this
items: You can distinguish the input workspace from the length of one answer.
scenes.note: Try it in Genesis. Pause for as long as you need. Continue when you can explain or confirm this result.

scenes.title:
A size that
really fits
scenes.body: Genesis checks model limits and local memory where possible.
scenes.note: Step 2 of 5 · Teaching 1 of 3. Locate the highlighted control.

scenes.title:
A size that
really fits
scenes.body: Trust my context window overrides some local safeguards; use it only when both the server and hardware support your chosen size.
scenes.note: Step 2 of 5 · Teaching 2 of 3. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
A size that
really fits
scenes.body: Context framing reserve keeps room for chat and tool formatting. Turning off the form’s context switch does not remove Genesis’s internal safe prompt budget.
scenes.note: Step 2 of 5 · Teaching 3 of 3. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
Match the
real capacity
items: Check what your model actually supports
Check the loaded server’s context
Check available RAM / graphics memory
Leave Trust my context window off unless verified
scenes.note: For Ollama, configure the loaded model/server separately. Genesis’s form alone does not enlarge that server window.

scenes.title:
Pause and
check this
items: The context choice agrees with your model and server.
scenes.note: Try it in Genesis. Pause for as long as you need. Continue when you can explain or confirm this result.

scenes.title:
Variation and
repetition
scenes.body: Temperature adjusts variation. Top-P and Top-K adjust which possible next words can be considered. Presence penalty and Repeat penalty affect repetition when supported.
scenes.note: Step 3 of 5 · Teaching 1 of 2. Locate the highlighted control.

scenes.title:
Variation and
repetition
scenes.body: These are optional fine-tuning controls. Keep the model’s recommended values until you have a specific problem to solve.
scenes.note: Step 3 of 5 · Teaching 2 of 2. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
Change one
thing at a time
items: Keep the model’s recommended starting values
Use the same short request for comparison
Change one supported control only
Save, inspect the result, then keep or undo
scenes.note: Temperature changes variation. Top-P/Top-K constrain choices. Repetition controls depend on provider support.

scenes.title:
Pause and
check this
items: You know what these controls broadly mean without needing to change them.
scenes.note: Try it in Genesis. Pause for as long as you need. Continue when you can explain or confirm this result.

scenes.title:
Reasoning and
streaming
scenes.body: The reasoning chooser appears according to the model’s abilities. Use profile follows the saved configuration; supported models may offer Off, Low, Medium or High.
scenes.note: Step 4 of 5 · Teaching 1 of 2. Locate the highlighted control.

scenes.title:
Reasoning and
streaming
scenes.body: Stream mode shows words as they arrive; off waits for a full reply. Streaming changes presentation, not whether Genesis can use tools.
scenes.note: Step 4 of 5 · Teaching 2 of 2. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
Choose effort
and presentation
items: Use profile: retain the saved reasoning behavior
Off / Low / Medium / High: only if supported
Stream on: display words as they arrive
Stream off: wait for the complete reply
scenes.note: Try the same small request with streaming on and off. Tools remain available; the display timing changes.

scenes.title:
Pause and
check this
items: You can choose a supported reasoning level and recognise streaming.
scenes.note: Try it in Genesis. Pause for as long as you need. Continue when you can explain or confirm this result.

scenes.title:
Profiles and
mood
scenes.body: Advanced thinking profiles and Custom reasoning levels describe provider-specific request settings.
scenes.note: Step 5 of 5 · Teaching 1 of 3. Locate the highlighted control.

scenes.title:
Profiles and
mood
scenes.body: Use the provider’s supported values; invented level names do not give a model new abilities.
scenes.note: Step 5 of 5 · Teaching 2 of 3. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
Profiles and
mood
scenes.body: Thinking follows mood, when enabled, adjusts effort within your selected ceiling for supported models. It does not add reasoning levels to a model that has none.
scenes.note: Step 5 of 5 · Teaching 3 of 3. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
A ceiling for
mood-based effort
items: Thinking follows mood starts off
On: effort responds to mood and kind of turn
It stays within your selected ceiling
Use profile uses High as the ceiling
scenes.note: Rested or flowing work can use more effort; tiredness or small talk less; resting can turn thinking off. Supported reasoning models only.

scenes.title:
Pause and
check this
items: You understand why some controls are unavailable for a particular model.
scenes.note: Try it in Genesis. Pause for as long as you need. Continue when you can explain or confirm this result.

scenes.title:
Keep a
backup ready.
scenes.body:
Keep going with a backup model
Test a second model and understand recovery.

scenes.title:
Before
you begin
items: Two working saved model presets. A local backup can work when a cloud service is unavailable.
scenes.note: These are the prerequisites for this lesson. Prepare them before you try the connection.

scenes.title:
Test both
models first
scenes.body: Connect and test your second model, then save it as a preset. A backup must be able to answer on its own.
scenes.note: Step 1 of 6 · Teaching 1 of 2. Locate the highlighted control.

scenes.title:
Test both
models first
scenes.body: Selecting an uninstalled local model or a cloud model without a valid key will not provide a working backup.
scenes.note: Step 1 of 6 · Teaching 2 of 2. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
Prove both
connections work
items: Choose the primary and send a short test
Choose the intended backup and test it too
Save both as their own presets
Return to the primary you want for everyday use
scenes.note: An uninstalled local model or cloud model with an invalid key cannot rescue the primary.

scenes.title:
Pause and
check this
items: Both the primary and backup have answered a small test.
scenes.note: Try it in Genesis. Pause for as long as you need. Continue when you can explain or confirm this result.

scenes.title:
Choose your
backup
scenes.body: Open Settings → Models → Companion failover — not Missions. Choose the second preset under Backup model and click Save changes.
scenes.note: Step 2 of 6 · Teaching 1 of 2. Locate the highlighted control.

scenes.title:
Choose your
backup
scenes.body: This covers Chat, Work, Autonomy and companion helpers. The compact Backup chooser below the Modern message box also selects a saved backup.
scenes.note: Step 2 of 6 · Teaching 2 of 2. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
A companion
backup example
items: Primary: your tested cloud preset
Backup: your tested local preset
Models → Companion failover → Backup model
Save changes; look for the standby status
scenes.note: The compact Backup chooser below the Modern draft also selects a saved backup. A cloud outage need not stop local replies.

scenes.title:
Pause and
check this
items: The backup status reports standby or current fallback use.
scenes.note: Try it in Genesis. Pause for as long as you need. Continue when you can explain or confirm this result.

scenes.title:
When fallback
can help
scenes.body: If the primary fails before delivering an answer—for example because of a provider usage limit, rate limit, timeout or outage—Genesis can retry through the configured backup.
scenes.callout: Using backup: Qwen3 8B (Ollama). Next request will retry primary.
scenes.note: Step 3 of 6 · Teaching 1 of 3. Locate the highlighted control.

scenes.title:
When fallback
can help
scenes.body: It carries the working request forward.
scenes.callout: Using backup: Qwen3 8B (Ollama). Next request will retry primary.
scenes.note: Step 3 of 6 · Teaching 2 of 3. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
When fallback
can help
scenes.body: Content or tool work already delivered is not blindly replayed on the backup, so fallback is not a promise that every partial failure can be recovered.
scenes.callout: Using backup: Qwen3 8B (Ollama). Next request will retry primary.
scenes.note: Step 3 of 6 · Teaching 3 of 3. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
Before versus
after delivery
items: Primary fails before answering: backup can retry
Example cause: rate limit, timeout or outage
The working request carries forward
Delivered content or tool work is not blindly replayed
scenes.note: A partial failure may require you to inspect what already happened. Fallback cannot promise recovery of every unfinished result.

scenes.title:
Pause and
check this
items: You recognise the backup status when the demonstration shows it.
scenes.note: Try it in Genesis. Pause for as long as you need. Continue when you can explain or confirm this result.

scenes.title:
Chosen versus
answering model
scenes.body: The primary’s saved connection remains your primary. The status explains which model is actually answering, separately from your chosen primary.
scenes.callout: Using backup: Qwen3 8B (Ollama). Next request will retry primary.
scenes.note: Step 4 of 6 · Teaching 1 of 2. Locate the highlighted control.

scenes.title:
Chosen versus
answering model
scenes.body: Your backup might be less capable: a smaller local model may give a simpler answer, and it may need a separate vision helper for pictures.
scenes.callout: Using backup: Qwen3 8B (Ollama). Next request will retry primary.
scenes.note: Step 4 of 6 · Teaching 2 of 2. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
Read both
model identities
items: Configured primary: your chosen cloud preset
Effective model during fallback: the local backup
The saved primary remains the same
Expect the backup’s own capabilities and limits
scenes.note: Illustrative fallback status. A smaller text-only model may answer more simply or need a separate vision helper for pictures.

scenes.title:
Pause and
check this
items: You can tell a configured primary from the effective backup.
scenes.note: Try it in Genesis. Pause for as long as you need. Continue when you can explain or confirm this result.

scenes.title:
Retry on a
real request
scenes.body: Retry primary after (minutes) is the cooldown. After it passes, the next real request tests the primary. Success returns to primary; failure starts another waiting period.
scenes.note: Step 5 of 6 · Teaching 1 of 2. Locate the highlighted control.

scenes.title:
Retry on a
real request
scenes.body: Genesis does not make a paid background ping just because the timer expires. A backend restart starts with the saved primary again.
scenes.note: Step 5 of 6 · Teaching 2 of 2. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
A 30-minute
cooldown example
items: 00:00 — recoverable primary failure uses backup
00:30 — timer passes; no paid background ping
Next actual request tries the primary
Success returns; failure starts another wait
scenes.note: The times are illustrative. A backend restart starts with the saved primary; timer expiry alone sends no test request.

scenes.title:
Pause and
check this
items: You understand why the status can say the next request will retry.
scenes.note: Try it in Genesis. Pause for as long as you need. Continue when you can explain or confirm this result.

scenes.title:
Mission roles
are separate
scenes.body: Open Settings → Missions → Role models for mission primary and backup choices. The companion backup does not govern Missions.
scenes.note: Step 6 of 6 · Teaching 1 of 2. Locate the highlighted control.

scenes.title:
Mission roles
are separate
scenes.body: Each role may use a different model and has its own failover window for provider rate limits. Check these before a big job.
scenes.note: Step 6 of 6 · Teaching 2 of 2. Read this before you change the setting.

scenes.title:
A useful
detail
items: Usage limits are different from a full context window or a task’s step budget.
A backup does not remove those other limits.
scenes.note: Keep this distinction in mind as you practice.

scenes.title:
Set the
mission roles too
items: Settings → Missions → Role models
Check each role’s own primary and backup
Roles can have different models and failover windows
Check this before starting a big mission
scenes.note: Companion backup covers Chat, Work, Autonomy and helpers. It does not replace mission role choices or remove context / step limits.

scenes.title:
Pause and
check this
items: You know where to set the mission’s independent model choices.
scenes.note: Try it in Genesis. Pause for as long as you need. Continue when you can explain or confirm this result.

complete

Return to any step with the lesson chapter
Continue when the checkpoint is clear

setup checklist
